techniques.title: Real-Time Conversational Stack (WebRTC, full vs lite)
techniques.what_it_does: A live-avatar session streams over WebRTC: the user's speech is transcribed, a language model generates a response, speech synthesis produces audio, and the avatar renders synchronized lip movement and expressions in real time. Two integration modes exist: full (the platform manages speech recognition, language model, synthesis, and rendering) and lite (the operator brings their own speech/language/ synthesis stack; the platform supplies only the avatar rendering layer).
techniques.why_it_works: The rendering layer is cleanly separable from the conversation stack. Full mode optimizes for speed of integration; lite mode optimizes for control — both share the same render endpoint.

techniques.title: Speaker Encoder → Embedding Pipeline
techniques.what_it_does: A speaker encoder (neural network trained on thousands of voices) extracts a compact speaker embedding from a short reference clip — the acoustic signature (tone, pitch distribution, formant structure, rhythmic pattern). An autoregressive transformer then generates speech tokens conditioned on the text AND the embedding; a vocoder converts tokens to waveform.
techniques.why_it_works: It decouples "who is speaking" (embedding) from "what is said" (text). The same embedding steers every utterance, so identity holds without retraining per sentence.
techniques.genesis_implementation: In the voice module, design the synthesis pipeline as: enrollment (record → encoder → store embedding) separate from rendering (text + embedding → tokens → waveform). Never bake the voice into the model weights for the instant tier; embeddings are lightweight, portable, and deletable (privacy + LAW compliance).

techniques.title: Two-Tier Cloning: Instant (embedding) vs Professional (fine-tuned)
techniques.what_it_does: Instant Voice Cloning (IVC) works off the embedding alone — ~10 seconds to ~2 minutes of audio, usable in seconds-to-a-minute. Professional Voice Cloning (PVC) fine-tunes a dedicated model on 30+ minutes of clean audio, taking ~3–6 hours, and captures breath patterns, micro-pauses, and emotional range far more faithfully.
techniques.why_it_works: Tiering trades fidelity for setup cost. Instant covers "try it now"; professional covers "this voice will speak for thousands of sentences." Rule of thumb from practitioners: use IVC to learn what the source recording captures, move to PVC when the quick clone can't hold the accent, timbre, or delivery for repeated use.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Voice module enrollment offers both: (1) fast path — few samples, embedding-only, immediate usability; (2) deep path — long recording session, fine-tuned model, QC'd before activation. A voice is marked `tier: instant | professional` in its metadata; the scheduler prefers professional-tier voices for long sessions (narration) and instant for experiments.

techniques.title: Inline Expression Tags (stage directions in text)
techniques.what_it_does: Writers put performance directions directly in the script in square brackets — e.g. `[laughs]`, `[whispers]`, `[sighs]`, `[said angrily in French accent]`, background cues like `[light rain]` — and the model performs them. Tags can be stacked and sequenced; v4 also exposes IPA phonetic control for exact pronunciation.
techniques.why_it_works: It moves direction from the settings panel into the writer's flow. The script IS the performance brief; a tag read in context lets the model adjust tone and pacing from surrounding text, not just from the tag.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Voice module script schema supports inline tags. The renderer's tag grammar is versioned and documented; unknown tags fail CLOSED (render without the tag + warn) rather than being hallucinated into random prosody. Teach the scheduler to generate tags for GENESIS's own speech — e.g. `[calm tone]` for reminders, `[warm tone]` for greetings.

techniques.title: Explicit Expressiveness Knobs (stability, similarity, style, speed)
techniques.what_it_does: Four sliders tune delivery per voice: stability (consistency vs. expressiveness), similarity boost (fidelity to the source voice), style exaggeration (amplifying the speaker's style, at added latency), speed (0.7–1.2 range; extremes degrade quality).
techniques.why_it_works: "One voice" is not one output — the same voice at stability 0.4 vs 0.8 serves different jobs (conversation vs. narration). Named presets exist per use case: narration (stability 0.5, style 0), conversational (0.4, style 0.3), cloned voice (similarity 0.85, style 0).
techniques.genesis_implementation: Voice module exposes these as per-job parameters with safe defaults and hard ranges. The scheduler selects the preset by intent: alerts → conversational; long-form reading → narration. Settings are logged per render so a QC failure can be traced to the exact knob combination.

techniques.title: Chunked WebSocket Streaming (sentence-boundary flush)
techniques.what_it_does: The TTS WebSocket (`stream-input` endpoint) accepts a space as Beginning-of-Stream, receives text chunks as they are generated, and emits base64 audio frames as each sentence boundary is reached (`. ? !`), never waiting for the full LLM output. Time-to-first-audio: ~150–300 ms with Flash v2.5; v4 Turbo speaks in ~150 ms.
techniques.why_it_works: The LLM and the vocoder overlap in time. Playing audio before the sentence is finished decouples perceived latency from total generation time — conversation feels real-time.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The voice module's conversational path runs on a persistent WebSocket with chunked text input and sentence-boundary flush. Pre-rendered narration (audiobooks, notifications) uses the cheaper REST path — the routing rule is REST vs streaming by interactivity need.

techniques.title: Context-Aware Multi-Segment Continuity
techniques.what_it_does: Long renders accept `previous_text` / `next_text` context hints around each chunk; v4 improved request stitching so voices keep their identity over chapters — the failure mode it fixes is voice drift across long passages.
techniques.why_it_works: Prosody is contextual — how a sentence starts depends on what came before. Stitching hints give the model the missing boundary information so adjacent chunks sound like one continuous performance.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Any long-form render in the voice module is generated as overlapping-window chunks with context hints, then cross-faded at stitch points. A QC check compares embedding distance across chunk boundaries; drift above threshold triggers a re-render of the join.

techniques.title: Voice Design from Text Description
techniques.what_it_does: A new voice is created from a text description plus structured attributes: gender (male/female/neutral), age (young/middle/old), accent (american, british, australian, indian, ...), accent strength (0.3–2.0). The system generates up to 3 previews from 20–1000 characters of preview text; the user saves the chosen one to their library.
techniques.why_it_works: It separates "what the voice sounds like" from any real person — no consent problem, no biometric data. Descriptions map to latent attributes the encoder already understands.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Voice module supports description-designed voices as the DEFAULT for non-personal voices (alerts, narration), keeping cloning for the father's voice only. Seed support for reproducible generation; the design record (description + attributes + seed) is stored so the voice can be exactly recreated.

techniques.title: Multilingual Identity-Preserving Dubbing
techniques.what_it_does: A cloned or designed voice keeps its timbre while speaking 90+ languages (v4; 70+ in v3) — a Spanish speaker's clone reading German sounds like that person with native German pronunciation, not an English speaker forcing it. One recording can be deployed across a whole catalogue.
techniques.why_it_works: The embedding encodes speaker identity independent of phoneme inventory; the model maps target-language phonetics onto the same acoustic signature.
techniques.genesis_implementation: For GENESIS's assistant, the father's voice (cloned with consent) can address him in whatever language context is active — English conversation, Persian terms read naturally — without re-enrolling per language. Practitioner gotcha to encode: language-matched voices must be enforced — English-trained voices forced into non-English cause pronunciation issues, so the language hint must always be explicit.

techniques.title: Consent + Identity Gates Before Any Cloning
techniques.what_it_does: Cloning requires consent verification — the uploader confirms rights/permissions. Professional Voice Cloning adds a stricter identity gate: only the speaker themselves can create and verify their own professional clone, even with third-party permission; only after they verify can they share access. Clones of some political figures are blocked outright.
techniques.why_it_works: It makes voice a first-class identity asset, not data. The gate is at creation time, before any model training — the cheapest point to stop abuse.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Voice module cloning entry requires a recorded spoken-consent phrase from the speaker, stored with the voice record. PVC-grade fine-tuning is available ONLY for the father's own voice, gated by his explicit per-case approval. This gate must be code-enforced (permission_gate pattern, hands), never UI-only.

techniques.title: Provenance Watermarking (detectable synthetic audio)
techniques.what_it_does: Every generation is digitally watermarked, with a public classifier that can flag audio made with the tool; back-tracking systems can identify the source and purpose of a voice clone. Claimed detection precision: 99% (vendor-reported).
techniques.why_it_works: Watermarks don't stop misuse — they stop DENIABILITY. Detection creates accountability for synthetic audio downstream.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Every audio file the voice module renders is watermarked + recorded in a provenance log (voice_id, model, timestamp, text hash, intended use). GENESIS's own classifier can verify "was this made by us?" — and critically, the 369 publish gate can detect AI voice and fail closed on it. Log retention policy: provenance records are permanent; raw text is not.

techniques.title: Chunked Long-Form Generation with Stitch Reliability
techniques.what_it_does: The TTS module caps single requests (~5,000 characters; v4 up to 10,000); long scripts are split at sentence/paragraph boundaries, queued sequentially, and stitched. Errors are fixed by re-rendering the failed paragraph only and splicing — a re-render does NOT repeat the whole chunk.
techniques.why_it_works: Failures are local; recovery is local. Mid-word splits introduce audible artefacts, so boundaries are sacred.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Voice module long-form pipeline: split → render chunk → QC each chunk → stitch → final QC. A per-chunk manifest (text hash → audio file → settings) lets re-renders target exactly the failing paragraph. Never re-render the whole script for one mispronounced word.

techniques.title: Pronunciation Dictionaries + SSML Pause Control
techniques.what_it_does: A custom pronunciation dictionary maps problem words (names, acronyms, serial numbers, brand terms) to phonetic spellings; SSML `<break time="1.5s"/>` gives precise pause control between sentences. Independent reviews confirm weak spots without these: mispronounced serial numbers, alphanumeric strings, acronyms, and names.
techniques.why_it_works: The model guesses pronunciation from orthography; the dictionary overrides the guess with certainty. Explicit pause tags beat punctuation for timing.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Voice module keeps a persistent pronunciation dictionary (seeded with the father's name, project names, "369", "GENESIS") applied automatically to every render. Long scripts are pre-scanned for acronyms/numbers and dictionary-checked before generation — fixing pronunciation BEFORE rendering saves credits and re-renders.

## Quality factors to design around (independently reported)

- Emotional flattening beyond ~200–250 words in one pass — chunk long scripts (T-11).
- Voice drift across chapters in long narration — stitch with context hints (T-06).
- Mispronounced serial numbers, alphanumeric strings, acronyms, proper names — pronunciation dictionary (T-12).
- Inconsistent adherence to inline performance tags — treat tags as hints with fallback neutral rendering, never as guaranteed.
- More material is not always better for instant clones — >3 min samples can reduce stability (T-02).
- Sample consistency beats sample quantity — one microphone, one room, one energy level.

workflows.title: Voice Enrollment (cloning the father's voice)
workflows.body:
The identity-gated onboarding for the one voice GENESIS will speak with.

1. **CONSENT** — The father records a spoken consent phrase (his voice,
   his words, naming the purpose). Stored with timestamp; required before
   anything else. Entry: explicit request to enroll a voice. Exit: consent
   recording exists, or the workflow stops (fail-closed).
2. **SAMPLE** — Record enrollment audio: 1–2 minutes of natural speech,
   one microphone, one room, consistent energy — varied pace, questions and
   statements. More material is NOT better; consistency beats quantity.
   Entry: consent on file. Exit: single-speaker, clean sample (no overlap,
   no background noise), or re-record.
3. **ENROLL** — Encoder extracts the speaker embedding; the voice record is
   created with tier=instant, consent reference, and source-consistency
   metadata. Exit: voice_id usable in any TTS call immediately.
4. **VERIFY** — Generate 3 test phrases (greeting, name of father, one
   acronym like "YPP"); the father listens and approves. Exit: father
   approval, or return to SAMPLE with notes.
5. **PROMOTE (optional, deep tier)** — If instant fidelity is insufficient
   for daily use: 30+ minutes of clean audio, fine-tuning run (hours),
   father's explicit per-case approval. Exit: tier=professional,
   QC'd on a long passage before activation.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Cloning someone else's voice | Consent recording is the speaker's own voice; mismatch = abort |
| Bad sample → bad clone forever | VERIFY stage listens before any real use |
| Voice used beyond consent scope | Consent names the purpose; new purpose = new consent |

workflows.title: TTS Production Pipeline (script → finished audio)
workflows.body:
The pipeline for any non-conversational speech (briefings, narration,
announcements).

1. **INTAKE** — Text + intent (narration / announcement) + target voice.
   Exit: script + intent + voice_id, all present.
2. **NORMALIZE (P-01)** — Expand acronyms/numbers, strip URLs, spell out
   everything to be spoken. Exit: script reads aloud cleanly by a human.
3. **PRE-FLIGHT (P-05)** — Scan for acronyms, names, numbers, brand terms;
   resolve through the pronunciation dictionary. Exit: zero un-resolved
   tokens.
4. **CHUNK (P-03)** — Split at paragraph/sentence boundaries; attach
   context hints (previous_text / next_text); write chunk manifest.
   Exit: chunks + manifest.
5. **RENDER** — Generate each chunk with the intent preset (P-04),
   direction tags (P-02), tier chosen by job (T-13). High-stakes jobs:
   three-take selection (P-07). Exit: all chunks rendered with manifests.
6. **STITCH + QC** — Concatenate with cross-fades at joins; QC checks:
   embedding distance across joins (drift), tag adherence, no artefacts,
   pauses natural. Re-render only failing paragraphs and splice.
   Exit: single audio file passing all QC checks.
7. **SEAL (P-08)** — Watermark + provenance log. Exit: provenance record
   complete; audio is marked synthetic and is rejected by the 369 publish
   gate.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Mispronounced acronym/serial | Pre-flight dictionary, not post-listen |
| Voice drift across chunks | Context hints + embedding-distance QC |
| Flat delivery over long scripts | Chunking ≤ ~200 words per pass + direction tags |
| Unlabeled synthetic audio leaking | Watermark-and-log is a mandatory stage, not optional |

workflows.title: Real-Time Conversational Loop (father talks, GENESIS answers)
workflows.body:
The low-latency voice loop for daily interaction.

1. **LISTEN** — Wakeword (wakeword module) → capture utterance; VAD
   endpoint detection; STT commit on silence. Exit: committed transcript.
2. **THINK** — LLM generates the reply; text streams chunk-by-chunk.
   Exit: text stream started.
3. **SPEAK** — Persistent TTS WebSocket; send space (BOS), stream text
   chunks as they arrive, flush audio at each sentence boundary
   (T-05). Flash-tier model for minimal latency. Exit: first audio
   chunk within the latency budget (~150–300 ms target).
4. **BARGE-IN** — If the father starts speaking, interrupt the current
   stream, close the context, and return to LISTEN. Exit: no overlapping
   speech beyond ~300 ms.
5. **LOG** — Transcript + audio provenance stored (P-08). Exit: session
   record complete.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Perceived latency kills the conversation | Streaming, not batch: audio plays before the full reply exists |
| GENESIS talks over the father | Barge-in with hard interrupt; speech never queues behind itself |
| Cloud voice dependency at runtime | Fallback: if the streaming service is unreachable, degrade to a
  local voice or text — never go silent |

workflows.title: Voice QC Loop (merciless review for audio)
workflows.body:
The audio analog of our LAW-050 merciless review, applied to every
high-stakes render.

1. **GENERATE** — Render per W-02 with settings manifest.
2. **LISTEN-BACK** — Independent check (not the scheduler that wrote the
   script): pronunciation of every dictionary token, tag adherence, pause
   naturalness, no robotic phrasing, no artefacts.
3. **SCORE** — Pass / fix-list. Fix-list names the exact chunk and the
   exact fault (e.g. "chunk 4, 'YPP' misread — dictionary entry missing").
4. **FIX** — Re-render only the failing chunk (paragraph-level splice),
   or add the missing dictionary entry and re-render. Never the whole
   script for one word.
5. **SEAL** — Watermark + provenance (P-08); verdict stored with the
   audio.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| The script-writer QC's its own audio | Independent listener; separation of roles |
| Same fault fixed twice | Every fix writes a dictionary or settings rule — never fix the same
  mispronunciation twice |
| AI voice leaking into published content | Seal stage marks synthetic provenance; 369 publish gate rejects it
  fail-closed |

techniques.title: Dual-Autoregressive Architecture (Slow semantic + Fast acoustic)
techniques.what_it_does: The synthesis model is split into two autoregressive transformers. A "Slow AR" stage generates high-level semantic tokens — what is being said and in what emotional register. A "Fast AR" stage then generates fine-grained acoustic tokens — the waveform-level detail that makes the voice sound like a specific person. The split is optimized so both stages run within the streaming budget.
techniques.why_it_works: Semantic intent and acoustic identity are different problems with different time constants. Decoupling them lets the system reason about expression at the Slow stage and about fidelity at the Fast stage, and lets each be tuned independently (expressiveness vs. latency) instead of compromising both in one monolithic pass.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Design the voice module's render path as two sequential stages: a semantic planner (text + direction tags → prosody/semantic token plan) followed by an acoustic renderer (plan + speaker reference → waveform). Keep a clean boundary between the two so prosody can be re-planned without re-rendering acoustics, and vice versa.

techniques.why_it_works: Directors think in words, not sliders. A natural-language direction layer removes the translation step between "say it like you're in a hurry" and the 12 parameter tweaks that currently approximate it.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Layer a director's-note field over the tag system: free-form English description → parsed into the same word-level tag stream (T-04) as a first-class input. This makes direction accessible to non-technical users (the father) without losing the precision of the tag layer underneath.

techniques.title: Native Multi-Speaker Dialogue in One Pass
techniques.what_it_does: The model generates interleaved multi-speaker dialogue in a single pass using `<|speaker:0|>`, `<|speaker:1|>`, … markers in the text, with one voice reference per speaker (`reference_id: [id0, id1]`). Turn dynamics (who speaks when, interruptions) are modeled natively, not by stitching separate single-speaker renders.
techniques.why_it_works: Stitched dialogue drifts: loudness, pace, breath, and room feel mismatch at every seam. Native generation keeps acoustic continuity and conversational dynamics consistent across turns.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Support a dialogue script format with speaker markers and per-speaker voice bindings as a first-class render mode in the voice module. Cross-voice acoustic continuity (matching pace/breath at turn boundaries) becomes a QC metric (see W-04).

techniques.title: Surgical Single-Word Regeneration
techniques.what_it_does: Drama 3 can reportedly fix a single word without regenerating the rest of a take — re-render only the bad word and drop it into the existing audio.
techniques.why_it_works: Full re-renders are expensive (compute + new seams + new QC surface). If the tokenizer boundary is clean and the acoustic context is re-supplied, a one-word patch is both cheaper and more consistent than a full take.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Build the render pipeline so every utterance keeps its token stream + reference context cached. A "patch word" API re-renders just the target word and splices it in, with an automatic seam check (loudness/pace/breath continuity on both sides). Full re-render is the fallback only when the patch fails QC.

techniques.title: Streaming With ~90 ms Time-to-First-Audio + Latency Tiers
techniques.what_it_does: The API reports roughly 90 ms time-to-first-audio on the standard endpoint (~70 ms on a single request) with selectable latency modes: normal (best quality) vs. balanced (~300 ms) for real-time use. Streaming works over HTTP chunks and WebSocket.
techniques.why_it_works: Conversational voice lives or dies on first-chunk latency. A two-tier latency contract lets the caller choose quality for narration and speed for dialogue instead of paying one mode's cost for the other's job.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The conversational voice path must expose `latency: normal | balanced` per request, stream audio in chunks, and target sub-500 ms first-audio on-device. Latency budget is a logged KPI per session (see W-03).

techniques.title: Rich-Transcription Round-Trip QC
techniques.what_it_does: A rich-transcription model (fine-tuned to transcribe words AND annotate vocal events/turns as natural-language instructions) is used during RL to re-transcribe generated audio and diff it against the original prompt — penalizing hallucinations, missing words, and ignored vocal instructions automatically.
techniques.why_it_works: It turns QC into a closed loop: generation → listen back (machine) → compare → score. Catches the most common TTS failure modes (skipped/repeated words, wrong emotion) without human ears.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Every non-trivial voice render passes through automatic round-trip transcription; word-error and instruction-adherence deltas are logged. A render that drops or adds words FAILS closed and is re-rendered before any human listens. This is the cheapest possible verify step (T-01 pattern from the Astra pack, applied to voice).

techniques.title: Voice Design From Text Description
techniques.what_it_does: A new voice can be created from a natural-language description (age, gender, tone, character) instead of a reference clip — "design" the voice, then use it like any cloned voice.
techniques.why_it_works: It removes the enrollment step entirely for use cases where no real person's voice is involved (characters, assistants, narration personas), and it makes voice selection a creative act rather than a library search.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Offer a `design` enrollment path: description → generated voice model → father audition (listen before activation). Designed voices are marked `origin: designed` and carry a permanent synthetic-provenance tag so the 369 publish gate can never mistake them for a real person's recording.

techniques.title: Open-Weight Core + Self-Hostability (data sovereignty)
techniques.what_it_does: Fish Speech / S1-mini weights are published open-source, so teams can self-host the models in their own VPC or air-gapped environments when data residency matters. The hosted API and the open weights coexist as two tiers of the same product.
techniques.why_it_works: Voice data is sensitive. For the father's own voice — the one voice GENESIS will speak with — the recording and the embedding should never have to leave his device. Open weights make "your voice never leaves your hardware" a real architecture, not a promise.
techniques.genesis_implementation: STRONG RECOMMENDATION for the voice module: default to a self-hosted/local inference path for the father's voice (station module owns the local runtime). Cloud API is a fallback the father must explicitly enable per case. Enrollment recordings and embeddings live on-device; sync only with his approval.

prompt_patterns.title: Write-For-Ears, Not For-Eyes
prompt_patterns.use_when: preparing any script GENESIS will speak.
prompt_patterns.pattern: A script that reads well silently usually speaks badly. Write short sentences, one idea per sentence, explicit punctuation for pauses. Numbers, acronyms, and symbols must be spelled as they should be spoken.
prompt_patterns.template: > Before any text reaches the renderer, normalize it: > "369" → "three six nine"; "YPP" → "Y P P"; "10:30" → "ten thirty"; > remove URLs, expand abbreviations via the pronunciation dictionary. > A script is render-ready only when a human could read it aloud cold.

- **Pattern:** A script that reads well silently usually speaks badly. Write
  short sentences, one idea per sentence, explicit punctuation for pauses.

- **Template:**

  > A script is render-ready only when a human could read it aloud cold.

prompt_patterns.title: Word-Level Direction Tags (emotion is a token)
prompt_patterns.use_when: the delivery needs emotion, pacing, or non-speech sounds on specific words.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Put the direction exactly where it belongs in the script, with bracket tags — read in context: `[warm tone]`, `[calm]`, `[whispers]`, `[laughs]`, `[sighs]`, `[emphasis]`, `[in a hurry]`, `[inhale]`, `[prolonged laugh]`. Tags attach to the word they follow or precede; a global preset is a last resort, never the default.
prompt_patterns.template: > `[warm tone] Good morning. [calm] Three items are ready for your decision > today. [emphasis] The second one cannot wait.` > Tags are hints, not guarantees — the renderer falls back to neutral > delivery for unknown tags and logs the miss (never invents prosody).

prompt_patterns.title: Speaker-Marked Dialogue Scripts
prompt_patterns.use_when: GENESIS must voice a multi-speaker scene (two assistant personas, a rehearsal, a summary of a conversation).
prompt_patterns.pattern: One script, one pass. Bind each voice once at the top, then mark turns inline: `<|speaker:0|>`, `<|speaker:1|>`, … Never write two separate scripts and stitch them — seams betray stitching.

prompt_patterns.title: Reference Clip Curation (one clip, one voice, finished sentence)
prompt_patterns.use_when: creating a zero-shot voice reference.
prompt_patterns.pattern: 15–30 seconds of clean speech, one microphone, one room, consistent energy. The clip's transcript must be EXACT (word-for-word), because the reference tokens anchor on it. End the clip on a finished sentence — a mid-sentence cut makes the clone leak the last word onto the start of every generated line. One reference per voice; reuse the same reference for every line of a session.
prompt_patterns.template: > Record → transcribe verbatim → trim to the last complete sentence → > check single-speaker, no overlap, no background music → register as the > voice's reference. Noisy room? Shorter and quieter beats longer and > noisier.

prompt_patterns.title: Patch-One-Word, Not Re-Render
prompt_patterns.use_when: a render has one mispronounced or mis-emphasized word.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Re-render ONLY the bad word with the original context, splice it in, and verify the seam: loudness, pace, and breath must match on both sides. Full re-render is the fallback only when the patch fails QC.
prompt_patterns.template: > `PATCH word #12 ("three-six-nine") → re-render with context ±5 words → > seam-check (loudness ±2 dB, pace continuity) → PASS → keep; FAIL → > full re-render.`

prompt_patterns.title: Normalize Before You Render (byte-aware)
prompt_patterns.use_when: any text enters the render queue, especially multilingual.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Normalization is a separate, inspectable stage: strip what cannot be spoken, expand what must be spelled, and compute the input byte count. Byte metering means non-ASCII languages cost more per word — the normalizer reports bytes in, expected seconds out, BEFORE the render runs, so cost is known up front.
prompt_patterns.template: > `INTAKE: text="…" → normalized="…" → 412 UTF-8 bytes → est. ~35 s > audio → render approved / exceeds budget → escalate to father.` --- ## Composition rule Scripts are composed in three layers, always in this order: **(1) P-08 normalize** the raw text, **(2) P-02/P-03 direction** (tags or director's note) on the normalized text, **(3) P-04/P-06 render strategy** (single voice, dialogue, or patch). **P-05** governs the voice reference and **P-07** governs the voice's legal existence — neither ever shares a stage with production rendering. workflows.title: Voice Enrollment (cloning the father's voice)
workflows.body:
The identity-gated onboarding for the one voice GENESIS will speak with.
Local/self-hosted path preferred (T-13).

1. **CONSENT** — The father records a spoken consent phrase (his voice, his
   words, naming the purpose: personal assistant). Stored with timestamp;
   required before anything else. Entry: explicit request to enroll a
   voice. Exit: consent recording exists, or the workflow stops
   (fail-closed).
2. **SAMPLE** — Record enrollment audio: 15–30 seconds of natural speech
   (P-05), one microphone, one room, consistent energy; transcribed
   verbatim; trimmed to the last complete sentence. Entry: consent on file.
   Exit: single-speaker, clean sample (no overlap, no background noise, no
   music), or re-record.
3. **REGISTER** — Encoder extracts reference tokens; the voice record is
   created with tier=instant, consent reference, scope, and
   visibility=private (P-07). Exit: voice_id usable in any TTS call
   immediately.
4. **VERIFY** — Generate 3 test phrases (greeting, father's name, one
   acronym like "YPP"); the father listens and approves. Entry: registered
   voice_id. Exit: father approval, or return to SAMPLE with notes.
5. **PROMOTE (optional, deep tier)** — If instant fidelity is insufficient
   for daily use: longer clean session, trained clone, father's explicit
   per-case approval. Exit: tier=trained, QC'd on a long passage before
   activation.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Cloning someone else's voice | Consent recording IS the speaker's voice; mismatch = abort |
| Bad sample → bad clone forever | VERIFY stage listens before any real use |
| Voice shared publicly by default | Visibility defaults to private; public is an explicit logged opt-in |
| Enrollment data leaves the device | Local path default; cloud fallback needs father's per-case approval |
| Voice used beyond consent scope | Consent names the purpose; new purpose = new consent |

workflows.title: TTS Production Pipeline (script → finished audio)
workflows.body:
The pipeline for any non-conversational speech (briefings, announcements,
narrations for the father).

1. **INTAKE** — Text + intent (briefing / announcement) + target voice_id
   + direction note. Entry: voice has a valid P-07 provenance header.
   Exit: intake accepted, or rejected (missing provenance = no render).
2. **NORMALIZE** — P-08 + P-01: strip unpronounceable content, expand
   numbers/acronyms, compute input byte count and cost estimate. Entry:
   intake accepted. Exit: render-ready script + byte cost, or escalation
   if over budget.
3. **DIRECT** — Compile direction (P-02 tags / P-03 director's note) onto
   the normalized script. Entry: render-ready script. Exit: directed
   script with inspectable tag stream.
4. **RENDER** — Generate via the two-stage path (T-01/T-02): semantic plan
   then acoustic render, chunked streaming for long text. Entry: directed
   script. Exit: raw audio.
5. **ROUND-TRIP QC** — Automatic re-transcription (T-11): diff words and
   vocal instructions against the prompt. Check the triple rubric (T-10):
   semantic accuracy, acoustic quality, speaker similarity. Entry: raw
   audio. Exit: PASS → delivery; FAIL → W-02 returns to RENDER (with
   P-06 patch-one-word first), never to delivery.
6. **DELIVER** — Final audio to the requesting module. Entry: QC PASS.
   Exit: delivered with QC report attached (word-error delta, bytes in,
   seconds out, render cost).

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Synthetic audio reaches 369 content | Provenance tag checked at delivery; publish gate fails closed on synthetic |
| Mispronunciations / skipped words ship | Round-trip QC fails closed; patch-before-rerender keeps cost down |
| Cost surprise on long renders | Byte count + estimate reported at NORMALIZE, before render |
| Wrong emotion lands on the wrong word | Tag stream is inspectable at DIRECT; QC checks instruction adherence |

workflows.title: Live Conversational Loop (streaming dialogue)
workflows.body:
The real-time voice path: the father speaks, GENESIS answers aloud with
low latency.

1. **LISTEN** — Capture the father's utterance (wakeword module hands off
   the turn). Entry: turn detected. Exit: audio chunk stream + end-of-turn
   signal.
2. **THINK** — Language model produces the reply text + a brief direction
   (tone of the reply). Entry: end-of-turn. Exit: reply text + direction,
   within the think budget.
3. **STREAM** — Render with `latency: balanced` (T-08), stream chunks as
   they arrive, target sub-500 ms time-to-first-audio. Entry: reply text
   ready. Exit: first chunk playing, or fallback escalation.
4. **TURN-TAKE** — Handle interruption: if the father speaks mid-reply,
   stop the stream, keep the cutoff transcript, and return to LISTEN with
   context preserved. Entry: new speech while streaming. Exit: clean stop
   + resume state.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Latency blows the conversational budget | Latency tier logged per turn; persistent misses escalate to shorter replies |
| Interruption loses the thread | Cutoff transcript is retained; next turn continues, not restarts |
| Render fails mid-stream | Fallback: finish the turn as text (chat), never as silence |
| Streaming cost spikes | Balanced-tier only for live turns; narration uses normal-tier (W-02) |

workflows.title: Multi-Character Dialogue Scene (single pass)
workflows.body:
For scenes GENESIS voices with more than one speaker (rehearsals,
summaries of conversations, character demos — father-facing only).

1. **CAST** — Bind each speaker to a voice (reference_id list); each voice
   has a valid provenance header (P-07). Entry: scene request. Exit:
   cast list, or stop if any voice lacks provenance.
2. **SCRIPT** — Write one script with `<|speaker:N|>` markers (P-04) plus
   word-level direction tags (P-02). Entry: cast list. Exit: single-pass
   script.
3. **RENDER-ONCE** — Native multi-speaker generation (T-06) in one pass.
   Entry: script. Exit: scene audio.
4. **SEAM QC** — At every turn boundary: loudness, pace, and breath
   continuity checked (T-07's seam check, generalized). Entry: scene
   audio. Exit: PASS → delivery; FAIL → P-06 patch the offending turn,
   re-check.
5. **DELIVER** — Scene audio + cast/QC report. Entry: QC PASS.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Stitched-sounding seams | Single-pass render; seam QC fails closed |
| A voice in the scene lacks consent | CAST stage stops before any render |
| One bad turn forces a full re-render | Patch-one-turn first (P-06 pattern), full re-render only on patch failure |
| Scene mistaken for real people's conversation | Provenance tags on every voice; never used in any public context |

## Cross-workflow invariants

1. **Provenance first:** no voice renders without a P-07 header — in any
   workflow, at any time.
2. **QC is automatic and fail-closed:** W-02 and W-04 never deliver on a
   failed check; W-03 degrades to text, never to silence or a broken take.
3. **Cost is known before it is spent:** byte metering at intake (W-02) and
   latency-tier choice per turn (W-03).
4. **The 369 publish gate sits OUTSIDE all of these workflows:** none of
   these stages has a path to published content. Any synthetic track
   reaching the gate is rejected — the gate is the last and separate
   line of defense.

workflows.body:
- **Entry criteria:** locked portrait asset (from W-02 or approved still);
  final script locked; voice decision made per standing law.
- **Steps:**
  1. Asset prep: crop to portrait spec, mouth visible, single face.
  2. Voice stage: TTS render per dialogue card (P-10) — OR, per NO AI VOICE
     law on 369: this stage is SKIPPED and the workflow becomes a
     captioned/motion treatment instead.
  3. Lip-sync bind: voice drives mouth; head motion stays within the
     expression model's range (wide moves and text-on-face route to the
     expression-motion path, per public walkthrough guidance).
  4. QC: mouth/face integrity on first, middle, last frame; no text over the
     mouth; export at target spec.
- **Exit criteria:** video passes frame QC; dialogue cards all rendered (or
  voice stage formally waived with reason); cost reconciled.
- **Guarded failure modes:**
  - Portrait has text over the mouth → reroute before animation; the lip-sync
    stage cannot fix a covered mouth.
  - Voice render sounds wrong → re-voice the single card, never the whole
    script (this is why the stages are decoupled).
  - Script longer than the animation model's ceiling → split across clips
    (two speakers max per clip is the public guidance); never stretch one
    clip past its model's range.

techniques.title: Voice as a Task Interface (not just chat)
techniques.what_it_does: Voice mode accepts spoken commands that trigger multi-step tasks (draft a doc, summarize messages), not just spoken Q&A. Work can start in voice on mobile and continue in text on desktop; if the task is still running when the voice call ends, it continues in text. Background conversations persist across apps.
techniques.why_it_works: It exploits dead time (walking, driving) for task initiation and decouples input modality from execution — the task doesn't die when the call does.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The voice module should accept task-level commands ("draft X", "check Y"), hand a structured job to the scheduler, and let the father continue or inspect it in text. Voice sessions must never be the only record: every voice-initiated task writes its transcript + job id to memory so the text side can resume it.

techniques.genesis_implementation: Add intent-shift detection to voice (and long chat sessions): track the current conversational mode (companionship / tasking / analysis / decision) and re-derive the response strategy when the inferred mode changes twice in a row. workflows.title: Voice-First Capture-to-Done
workflows.body:
For hands-free task initiation (T-11, P-09).

1. **CAPTURE** — Father speaks a task command. Voice transcribes and parses
   intent.
   Exit: transcript + parsed intent exist.
2. **STRUCTURE** — Intent becomes a scheduler job with goal, constraints,
   budget. The written record (transcript + job id) is stored to memory
   immediately.
   Exit: job registered; text side can see it.
3. **EXECUTE** — Job runs in text (scheduler + hands). The voice call may
   end; the job continues independently.
   Exit: result or blocker with evidence.
4. **RESUME** — Father continues in text or a later voice call; the system
   presents status from the written record, never from voice memory alone.
   Exit: father confirms outcome or issues corrections (which update the
   job, W-03 amend rule).
5. **MODE CHECK** — After intent shifts (T-12): re-derive the conversational
   mode and adjust response strategy; log the transition.
   Exit: response strategy matches the current mode.

Guarded failure modes: task dies with the call (STRUCTURE decouples them),
voice-only state lost (written record is the source of truth), mode drift
(MODE CHECK detector).

| W-03 | Misunderstood schedule firing silently | Confirm-before-live + hub visibility |
